facts.label: Perguntar ao professor
facts.sub: Levante a mão, diga “Excuse me”, pergunte o significado de uma palavra e peça para repetir com educação.

facts.label: Pedir a vez
facts.sub: Em muitas escolas dos EUA, o aluno levanta a mão e espera o professor chamar. Depois diz “Excuse me” e faz a pergunta. Em turmas menores, o professor pode aceitar perguntas a qualquer momento.

facts.label: Pedir para repetir
facts.sub: Professores costumam gostar quando você pede para repetir, porque isso mostra interesse. Use “Can you repeat, please?” ou “Slowly, please”. Não precisa pedir desculpas muitas vezes; uma vez, com um sorriso, é suficiente.

compare.br: In Brazil, many students call the teacher “professor” or “tia” and may wait for the teacher to finish before they speak.
compare.us: In the USA, students often call the teacher Mr., Ms. or Mrs. plus the last name, and questions in class are welcome in many schools.
compare.tip: Start with “Excuse me” and the name: “Excuse me, Ms. Lee.”
compare.ask: What do you say in your language when you do not understand? Say it in English.

pages.title: Lia’s big question · 1/3
paragraphs: Lia is a student in an English class in **San Antonio**. The class is new for her, and she feels **so lost**. Her teacher, Ms. Lee, writes a new word on the board: “homework.”

Lia raises her hand. “**Excuse me, teacher. I have a question.**” “**Of course. What is it?**” Ms. Lee asks. “**What does “homework” mean?**” “**It’s work you do at home**,” says the teacher. “**Ah, I see. Thank you.**”

pages.title: Lia’s big question · 2/3
paragraphs: Ms. Lee looks at the class. “**Any questions?**” Lia raises her hand again. “**Can you repeat, please?**” “**Sure. Slowly this time.**” Ms. Lee says the sentence again, one word at a time. “**Now it’s clear**,” Lia says. “**Don’t worry**,” says Ms. Lee. “**It gets easier.**”

Then Ms. Lee tells an old story, “The Boy Who Cried Wolf.” A boy shouts “Wolf!” as a joke, and the people run to help him. But there is no wolf. Later a real wolf comes, and nobody believes the boy. “In class, a real question is a good thing,” Ms. Lee says. “**Ask the teacher** anytime.”

pages.focus: o som do th em this, think, thank
pages.title: Laboratório de sons · o som
pages.what: O th inglês não existe em português. Brasileiros costumam trocá-lo por t, d ou f, e “this” soa como “dis” e “thank” como “tank”.
pages.how: Coloque a ponta da língua levemente entre os dentes e deixe o ar sair. Em “this” a garganta vibra (som sonoro); em “thank” só sai ar (som surdo).
pages.tip: Olhe no espelho: se você não vê a ponta da língua, o th ainda não saiu.
